scope_note: A sourced comparison of voice-agent orchestration frameworks and hosted platforms — what assembles ASR, an LLM, and TTS into a working pipeline, plus turn-taking. Turn-taking behavior itself (interruption handling, semantic VAD) is covered on the Turns page; several tools appear on both pages by design, each scoped to a different slice of the same tool.
method_note: Every claim is checked against the vendor's own documentation, source repository, or pricing page before publication, then adversarially audited in a second pass that actively tries to refute each field rather than confirm it. Where a figure could not be verified, the row says so in its `watch` field rather than omitting the caveat.

systems.name: Pipecat
systems.price_note: $0 for the framework itself (BSD-2-Clause, fully self-hostable). Optional managed Pipecat Cloud is metered separately: agent-1x $0.01/active-min ($0.0005/min reserved), PSTN $0.018/min, Daily WebRTC voice-only free for 1:1 sessions.
systems.transport: WebRTC (Daily, LiveKit, Vonage, or the built-in SmallWebRTCTransport), WebSocket (FastAPI/plain server), and telephony serializers for Twilio, Telnyx, Plivo, Vonage, Exotel, and WhatsApp.
systems.tool_calling: Function-calling across OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini and other supported LLM services, via Pipecat's own schema translated per-provider through adapters (with a custom_tools escape hatch for provider-native definitions). Pipecat Flows separately layers on structured multi-step conversations as a graph of nodes. Agent handoff, parallel fan-out, and sidecar processes are provided by a distinct Subagents framework (formerly the standalone pipecat-subagents repo, now folded into core Pipecat) — not part of Flows itself.
systems.self_host: Fully self-hostable under BSD-2-Clause; Daily's Pipecat Cloud is an optional managed-hosting add-on, never a requirement.
systems.best_for: Teams that want the widest selection of ASR/LLM/TTS/transport integrations and are comfortable assembling a Python pipeline themselves.
systems.watch: The framework is $0, but almost every real deployment still pays Daily's Pipecat Cloud per-minute rates for WebRTC/telephony hosting (agent-1x $0.01/active-min, PSTN $0.018/min) unless you run your own WebRTC/SIP infrastructure — budget for that even though the framework line item is free.
systems.standout: Largest integration library and broadest transport support of any framework surveyed, with near-daily commits and a v1.0 reached in April 2026.
systems.architecture: Composable, pipeline-based: ordered frame processors handle audio in, LLM, and audio out; agents can hand off, fan out, or run as sidecars over a shared bus, locally or distributed.
systems.observability: OpenTelemetry tracing integration; Sentry error-tracking support.
systems.sdk_languages: Server: Python. Client SDKs: JavaScript/React/React Native, Swift (iOS), Kotlin (Android), C++, ESP32.
systems.runs_on: Any Python-capable server; client SDKs target browser, mobile, and embedded (ESP32) targets.
systems.integration: Pluggable turn-detection (VAD plus an optional LLM-based turn detector), not a single fixed mechanism.
systems.adoption: 13,400+ GitHub stars, 2,300+ forks, 130+ contributors as of mid-2026

systems.name: LiveKit Agents
systems.licence: Apache-2.0 (agents framework and self-hostable LiveKit media server); the bundled turn-detector model weights ship under the separate LiveKit Model License, not Apache-2.0.
systems.price_note: $0 to self-host the framework and LiveKit server (Apache-2.0). LiveKit Cloud: Build plan $0/mo (1,000 agent-session min, 5 concurrent sessions), Ship from $50/mo (5,000 min), Scale from $500/mo (50,000 min); usage beyond allotment is $0.0100/agent-session-min plus separately metered per-model STT/TTS/LLM rates.
systems.transport: WebRTC for agent-to-user media; HTTP and WebSocket to backend systems; built-in SIP for inbound/outbound telephony.
systems.tool_calling: Tool/function calling compatible with any supported LLM, including forwarding tool calls to the frontend; structured multi-agent handoffs (e.g. a medical-triage-to-specialist pattern) for breaking workflows into stages.
systems.self_host: Fully self-hostable, including the LiveKit media server itself; LiveKit Cloud is an optional managed alternative.
systems.best_for: Teams that need production-grade WebRTC/SIP infrastructure bundled with the agent framework, not just an orchestration layer on top of someone else's transport.
systems.watch: The turn-detector model bundled with Agents ships under a separate LiveKit Model License, not Apache-2.0 — free to use inside LiveKit sessions, but the license restricts using or benchmarking it outside that context and auto-terminates on breach, so 'the framework is Apache-2.0' doesn't mean every shipped component is unrestricted.
systems.standout: Only framework surveyed that also ships its own production WebRTC media server and native SIP telephony as part of the same open-source stack.
systems.architecture: Stateful realtime agent servers register with LiveKit, receive dispatch requests, and spawn job subprocesses that join rooms as full participants.
systems.observability: LiveKit Cloud provides built-in observability with transcripts and traces for deployed agents; self-hosted deployments must instrument their own.
systems.sdk_languages: Python and Node.js.
systems.runs_on: Self-hosted LiveKit server (Docker/Kubernetes) or LiveKit Cloud.
systems.integration: Pluggable turn-detection (VAD plus an optional contextual turn-detector model).

systems.name: Vocode
systems.price_note: $0, free and open source (MIT); telephony/LLM/TTS provider usage is billed separately by those vendors.
systems.transport: Telephony (inbound/outbound calls, Zoom dial-in) via a self-hosted telephony server, built on a WebSocket-based streaming architecture; WebRTC is also documented via a LiveKit integration (docs/open-source/livekit-webrtc.mdx) -- the docs state agents are compatible with both WebRTC and WebSockets.
systems.tool_calling: An action framework lets the LLM trigger predefined actions (e.g. transferring a call) during a conversation; this predates modern multi-agent/handoff patterns.
systems.self_host: Self-hosted telephony server documented; no managed cloud offering from the project itself.
systems.best_for: Small proof-of-concept phone-call agents where a lightweight, permissively-licensed Python library is enough and you don't need active upstream development.
systems.watch: The GitHub repo's most recent commit is from November 2024, and the project describes itself as actively looking for community maintainers — treat it as effectively dormant, not a framework to build a new production system on.
systems.standout: One of the earliest open-source voice-LLM libraries; a simple, unopinionated Python API.
systems.architecture: Modular Python library with pluggable transcription, LLM, and synthesis service abstractions.
systems.sdk_languages: Python (primary); a separate React SDK exists.
systems.runs_on: Self-hosted Python server plus a self-hosted telephony server.

systems.name: TEN Framework
systems.licence: Apache-2.0 plus additional restrictions: no hosting the framework on end-user or mobile devices, and no deployment that competes with Agora's own offerings.
systems.price_note: $0 to self-host the framework; the framework itself has no separate managed-cloud SKU. However, Agora — the project's corporate steward, and the entity whose no-compete clause is baked into the licence — separately sells 'Conversational AI Engine,' a hosted product built on TEN and billed per participant-minute (~$0.10/min after a free tier). Third-party services the framework wires in directly (Agora RTC, LLM/ASR/TTS providers) are billed by those vendors.
systems.transport: WebRTC via Agora RTC, WebSocket, and telephony/SIP (e.g. Twilio) through example extensions.
systems.tool_calling: LLM integrations (OpenAI, etc.) support function calling within TEN's graph nodes.
systems.self_host: Self-hostable via Docker/Docker Compose; requires an Agora API key for the default RTC transport layer.
systems.best_for: Teams that want to describe an agent as a visual graph of STT/LLM/tool/memory nodes rather than write an imperative pipeline in code.
systems.watch: The license is Apache-2.0 plus custom clauses that forbid deploying TEN on end-user or mobile devices and forbid any use that competes with Agora's own offerings — read those before assuming this is unrestricted open source, especially for an edge/on-device deployment.
systems.standout: Graph-based visual orchestration (TMAN Designer) is a different authoring model from the pipeline-code approach every other framework here uses.
systems.architecture: Graph-based: STT/LLM/tool/memory nodes composed visually (TMAN Designer) or via config and executed by the TEN runtime, rather than an imperative code pipeline.
systems.sdk_languages: Python, TypeScript/Node.js, Go; C++ core.
systems.runs_on: Docker Compose; documented minimum 2 CPU cores / 4GB RAM plus Node.js LTS v18+.

systems.name: Rasa
systems.licence: Apache-2.0 for the legacy Rasa Open Source (NLU/Core) package; the current CALM approach requires Rasa Pro, which is proprietary/source-available under a free but capped Developer Edition license.
systems.price_note: $0 Developer Edition: one bot, capped at 1,000 external / 100 internal conversations per month, community-forum support only. Paid Business and Enterprise tiers remove the cap and add Rasa Studio, Kubernetes support, and premium support (custom pricing).
systems.transport: Channel connectors rather than raw WebRTC/WebSocket; voice specifically via a reference web voice-interface project plus third-party telephony/ASR/TTS connectors.
systems.tool_calling: CALM's flow/action system lets an LLM select and fill in developer-defined 'flows' backed by code-defined actions, rather than open-ended function calling — dialogue control deliberately stays in code.
systems.self_host: Self-managed on-prem or private-cloud deployment supported for Pro/Business tiers, plus a fully managed alternative.
systems.best_for: Teams that want deterministic, auditable dialogue control (business logic stays in code) with an LLM handling only language understanding — e.g. regulated voice IVR flows.
systems.watch: The CALM approach most people mean today when they say 'Rasa' runs on Rasa Pro, not the Apache-2.0 open-source package — the free Developer Edition license caps you at 1,000 external conversations/month before you need a paid plan.
systems.standout: CALM deliberately keeps business-critical actions in code instead of letting the LLM improvise them, trading flexibility for predictability and auditability.
systems.architecture: Dialogue-flow/state-machine: with CALM, the LLM handles language understanding while flows and code-defined actions handle control logic.
systems.sdk_languages: Python.

systems.name: Bolna
systems.price_note: $0, open-source orchestration package (MIT) is free to self-host; Bolna also sells a hosted API/dashboard built on the same OSS package.
systems.transport: Telephony-first: Twilio, Plivo, and Exotel are implemented telephony providers (confirmed in code and in Bolna's hosted Exotel integration guide) — the OSS README's 'Exotel (coming soon)' note is stale, dating to before Exotel's provider handlers shipped in Feb 2025. Vonage remains genuinely unimplemented/coming soon. FreeSWITCH and SIP-trunk are also supported but undocumented in most summaries. Bidirectional WebSocket streaming.
systems.tool_calling: Bolna does not natively send emails/SMS or book calendar entries. On call-end it fires a generic webhook (and supports custom outbound HTTP tool/function calls mid-conversation via its function-calling helper); turning that into an actual email, text, or calendar booking requires wiring the webhook to a third-party automation platform such as Make.com, which performs the action using its own modules.
systems.self_host: Docker Compose self-host setup (telephony server, Bolna server, Redis, plus ngrok for local dev).
systems.best_for: Getting a single telephony voice agent (inbound/outbound phone calls) live quickly without building the ASR/LLM/TTS/telephony wiring yourself.
systems.watch: It's telephony-first, not a general WebRTC/browser agent framework. Also note the OSS README understates current provider support (it still marks Exotel as 'coming soon' though Exotel shipped in code and hosted docs over a year ago) and omits FreeSWITCH/SIP-trunk, which are also implemented — only Vonage is genuinely unshipped. Post-call actions like email/SMS are not native; they require a separate Make.com (or similar) automation on top of Bolna's webhook.
systems.standout: Opinionated, config-driven (JSON) setup gets a phone-call agent running the fastest of the frameworks surveyed, at the cost of flexibility.
systems.architecture: Orchestration layer with pluggable ASR (Deepgram, Azure), LLM (OpenAI, DeepSeek, Llama, others via LiteLLM), and TTS (ElevenLabs, AWS Polly, Deepgram, Cartesia, others) providers, configured declaratively via JSON rather than coded as a pipeline.
systems.sdk_languages: Python; REST API.

systems.name: Dograh
systems.price_note: $0 to self-host (BSD-2-Clause) with bring-your-own API keys, or use the bundled default LLM/STT/TTS stack; a managed cloud option also exists for teams that don't want to self-host.
systems.transport: Telephony via Twilio, Vonage, Telnyx, Plivo, Vobiz, Cloudonix, and Asterisk ARI; browser-based audio for in-app testing.
systems.tool_calling: MCP-native: ships its own MCP server and supports tool-calling workflow nodes, including connecting MCP clients like Claude Code or Cursor.
systems.self_host: Single Docker-Compose command self-hosts the full stack, including bundled MinIO object storage.
systems.best_for: Teams that want a visual workflow builder in the style of Vapi/Retell but need it self-hosted and open source.
systems.watch: It's a young, fast-moving project — verify production-readiness for your scale before committing, and note its default telemetry is opt-out rather than opt-in (set ENABLE_TELEMETRY=false to disable).
systems.standout: The only framework surveyed pairing a visual workflow builder with native MCP support, positioning it as a self-hosted Vapi/Retell replacement rather than a code-first library.
systems.architecture: Visual no-code/low-code workflow builder (start/agent/QA/knowledge-base/webhook nodes) over a Python backend.
systems.sdk_languages: Python and Node.js client SDKs.

systems.name: OpenVoiceOS (OVOS)
systems.price_note: $0, fully free and open source; no managed cloud offering.
systems.transport: Local microphone/speaker input by default; network-capable for remote skills and LLM backends. No built-in WebRTC or telephony/SIP transport.
systems.tool_calling: Primarily intent/skill matching, not LLM tool-calling, by default. The optional ovos-persona plugin bridges to any OpenAI-compatible LLM (OpenAI, Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM) as a fallback layer, including a synthetic tool-call context-injection mode.
systems.self_host: Runs standalone (pip install ovos-core) or as a full device image for Raspberry Pi and other embedded/buildroot targets; fully local by design, no backend server required.
systems.best_for: Fully offline/edge smart-speaker-style assistants where privacy and running without a cloud LLM matter more than open-ended conversational flexibility.
systems.watch: It's an intent/skill-matching platform first and an LLM orchestrator second — the LLM layer (ovos-persona) is an optional fallback plugin, not the primary conversation engine, so don't expect general-purpose LLM tool-calling out of the box the way Pipecat or LiveKit Agents provide it. Also, the default STT engine still requires an internet connection despite the edge/offline positioning; local STT needs separate configuration.
systems.standout: Direct open-source successor to Mycroft, purpose-built for headless/embedded smart-speaker hardware rather than browser or telephony agents.
systems.architecture: Skill-based intent-matching pipeline with pluggable 'solver' plugins for fallback/LLM responses.
systems.sdk_languages: Python.
systems.runs_on: Raspberry Pi 3B+ and other embedded boards, Linux desktop, Docker; a dedicated buildroot image for headless devices.
systems.adoption: 283 GitHub stars, 31 forks on ovos-core (verified via GitHub API, last pushed August 4, 2026) — a small count next to Pipecat, TEN Framework, or LiveKit Agents, consistent with a niche embedded/smart-speaker successor project rather than a mainstream framework.

systems.name: Home Assistant Assist
systems.price_note: $0, fully free and open source, self-hosted as part of Home Assistant Core; an optional paid Home Assistant Cloud add-on (~$6.50/mo or $65/yr via Nabu Casa) offers remote access, Alexa/Google Assistant integration, and cloud STT/TTS. Cloud LLM conversation agents (e.g. OpenAI, Google Gemini) are a separate, free Home Assistant integration requiring the user's own API key with that provider — not part of, or billed through, the Cloud add-on.
systems.transport: Local network only by default — the Wyoming protocol (a small TCP-based standard) connects satellite STT/TTS/wake-word services to the Assist pipeline; optional cloud fallback for more capable models.
systems.tool_calling: Native LLM tool-calling via the Assist API: only models that support tool/function calling can control Home Assistant, and integrations expose tools (turn on lights, set thermostats, run scripts, check sensors) through an async_get_tools hook.
systems.self_host: Runs fully on your own hardware; this is the default and primary deployment model, not an add-on.
systems.best_for: Home-automation voice control where the agent needs to reliably operate a fixed, well-defined set of smart-home tools locally, not carry open-ended conversation.
systems.watch: This is a voice pipeline built into a home-automation platform, not a general-purpose conversational-agent framework — it's scoped to controlling Home Assistant entities via the Assist API's tool set, and building a non-home-automation voice agent on it works against the grain of the project.
systems.standout: The only fully local, zero-cloud-dependency option surveyed with a first-party LLM tool-calling integration (Assist API) rather than a bolted-on plugin.
systems.architecture: Pipeline: wake word to STT (Whisper or Speech-to-Phrase) to intent/LLM conversation agent (Assist API) to TTS (Piper), stages connected over the Wyoming protocol.
systems.sdk_languages: Python for integrations; Wyoming protocol clients can be written in any language.
systems.runs_on: Any Home Assistant Core install (Raspberry Pi, mini-PC, Docker, HAOS); ESPHome/ESP32 for satellite voice hardware.
systems.adoption: Not established from the sources reviewed — the cited source_url (home-assistant.io/voice_control/) contains no adoption figures, and the actual analytics data (analytics.home-assistant.io) could not be independently confirmed via direct primary-source access.

systems.name: Mycroft AI (mycroft-core)
systems.price_note: Was free and open source; the project and its hosted backend are discontinued, so there is nothing left to price.
systems.transport: Local microphone input; historically relied on a cloud backend (mycroft.ai) for some STT/skill services, which is no longer operational.
systems.tool_calling: Intent/skill-based (Adapt and Padatious intent parsers); no LLM tool-calling — this predates the current LLM-agent generation.
systems.self_host: Was self-hostable, but mycroft-core is archived and, per its own README, will likely not work on a current machine without patching.
systems.best_for: Historical reference only — do not start a new project on it.
systems.watch: The repository was archived by MycroftAI on GitHub (read-only, no further updates) on September 8, 2024, after the company ceased development in 2023 following a patent-troll lawsuit; its own README says it probably will not work on your computer anymore. Its spiritual successors are OpenVoiceOS and Neon AI.
systems.architecture: Skill-based intent matching (Adapt/Padatious), predating LLM-based orchestration.
systems.sdk_languages: Python.

systems.name: Vapi
systems.price_note: Build plan: $0.05/min platform fee plus pass-through STT/LLM/TTS costs at provider cost (or $0 if you bring your own API key); Scale plan adds a fixed platform fee with committed-volume per-minute pricing; add-ons: $2,000/mo HIPAA BAA, $1,000/mo zero-data-retention.
systems.transport: WebRTC via Web/mobile SDKs, native phone numbers over PSTN, SIP trunking to existing telephony, plus a WebSocket path for custom transports.
systems.tool_calling: Native function-calling with JSON-schema tool definitions and server-side webhook execution, plus a dedicated handoff tool for routing between assistants inside a Squad.
systems.self_host: Managed cloud (primary/default); a separate on-premises licence is available for enterprise, keeping audio/text off Vapi's servers.
systems.best_for: Developer teams that want full API/SDK control over a voice pipeline (model choice, prompts, tool wiring, multi-agent handoff) without operating STT/LLM/TTS infrastructure themselves.
systems.watch: The advertised $0.05/min is the orchestration fee only. STT/LLM/TTS/telephony are billed on top at provider cost, and independent cost breakdowns put a real production minute closer to $0.15-0.30+ once every layer is stacked; enterprise budgets commonly land in the $40k-70k/year range.
systems.standout: Squads: natively composable multi-assistant handoff for splitting one workflow across several specialized agents while preserving conversation context.
systems.architecture: Single assistants for simple flows; Squads (multiple specialized assistants linked by a handoff tool) for multi-step/multi-specialist flows, built via a visual workflow builder or the full API.
systems.observability: Boards (custom analytics dashboards), automatic per-call analysis/summarization, Evals for regression-testing prompts/tools/handoffs, and Monitoring for threshold-based quality alerts.
systems.sdk_languages: Web/JavaScript, React Native, Flutter, iOS (Swift), Python, a vanilla HTML embed, and a full REST API.
systems.runs_on: Fully managed multi-region cloud; on-premises deployment available for enterprise compliance needs.
systems.integration: Bring-your-own STT/LLM/TTS providers (Deepgram, AssemblyAI, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, ElevenLabs, and others) or use Vapi's bundled defaults.

systems.name: Retell AI
systems.price_note: Usage-based, no platform fee: ~$0.055/min voice infrastructure + ~$0.015/min TTS + $0.003-0.16/min LLM (model-dependent) + ~$0.015/min telephony, i.e. roughly $0.07-0.31/min all-in; $10 free trial credit; phone numbers $2/mo, SMS $20/mo, knowledge bases $8/mo (first 10 free), 20 free concurrent calls then $8/concurrency/mo.
systems.transport: Native phone numbers over PSTN, SIP trunking into any existing telephony/PBX/contact-center stack (Twilio, Vonage, Amazon Connect, Avaya, Genesys, Five9, Telnyx), plus WebRTC/web-call SDKs.
systems.tool_calling: Real-time function calling for booking, payments, record updates, and human call transfer, plus streaming RAG for knowledge-base lookups with auto-sync.
systems.self_host: Fully managed cloud only. Retell's own support team confirmed (community forum, Apr 25 2026) that on-premises deployment is not currently offered and data residency is not configurable; enterprise customers get contractual/compliance accommodations and on-premise SIP-trunk connectivity (BYOC into an existing PBX), not a deployable on-prem AI processing stack.
systems.best_for: Teams that want a fast path from an existing telephony/CRM stack to a production voice agent, with published low-latency numbers and no platform-fee floor to get started.
systems.watch: The headline $0.07/min covers voice infrastructure only; TTS/LLM/telephony are billed as separate line items on top, and Retell's own pricing breakdown shows the realistic range running to $0.31/min depending on which LLM backs the agent.
systems.standout: Multi-prompt agents split a conversation into a tree of per-state prompts and tools rather than one long system prompt. Retell's own documentation frames this as solving the tool-reliability and prompt-complexity problems single-prompt agents hit past roughly 5 functions or 1000 words ('unreliable tool usage with multiple functions' vs. 'better function control'); no published, measured hallucination-reduction figure was found to support that specific claim.
systems.architecture: Single-prompt agents for simple flows, or multi-prompt agents (a tree of per-state prompts with deterministic transition rules) for complex ones, built via a drag-and-drop flow editor or the full REST API.
systems.observability: Post-call analysis and QA scoring, call transcription/recording, batch-calling and call-transfer tooling for high-volume operations, plus a public changelog documenting platform behavior.
systems.sdk_languages: Official Node.js/TypeScript and Python SDKs, a client-side JS SDK for web calls, and a full REST API.
systems.runs_on: Fully managed cloud, hosted in a single AWS region (US-West-2 Oregon) as of April 2026, with EU regions stated as planned later in the year; no confirmed on-premises deployment of the voice AI pipeline itself — only on-premise SIP trunk connectivity for enterprise telephony integration.
systems.integration: Open API connects into existing telephony/CRM stacks (Twilio, HubSpot, Salesforce, Zapier, Make, n8n) rather than locking a customer into one bundled stack; uses a proprietary turn-taking model rather than a named pluggable VAD.

systems.name: Bland AI
systems.price_note: Tiered: Start = $0/mo platform fee + $0.14/min talk time (no card required); Build = $299/mo + $0.12/min; Scale = $499/mo + $0.11/min; Enterprise = custom, unlimited concurrency. LLM/STT/TTS are included in the per-minute rate with no separate token charges.
systems.transport: Native phone numbers, SIP, and contact-center integrations (Genesys, Five9, NICE CXone, Talkdesk, Amazon Connect, Twilio), plus SMS/iMessage/web-chat channels sharing one memory.
systems.tool_calling: Custom API/webhook actions plus prebuilt integrations (Salesforce, HubSpot, Calendly, Cal.com, Slack, Notion, Zapier, Make, Pipedream), triggered from individual pathway nodes.
systems.self_host: Managed cloud by default; Enterprise tier adds dedicated infrastructure and on-prem/VPC deployment with US/EU/APAC data residency.
systems.best_for: Regulated or enterprise call centers that want a no-code, flowchart-style builder with white-glove implementation, trading a monthly platform fee for higher concurrency and lower per-minute rates at volume.
systems.watch: Free credits and a card-free Start tier make it easy to prototype, but real production concurrency sits behind $299-499/mo platform fees on top of usage; comparison posts quoting a flat $0.09-0.11/min are citing the higher-volume Scale tier, not the entry price.
systems.standout: Conversational Pathways: a no-code, flowchart-style node builder (branching on conditions, external API calls, knowledge-base lookups) built for non-developers designing multi-step call logic, rather than one long prompt.
systems.architecture: Node-based "Pathways": a flowchart of discrete conversation nodes (greeting, data collection, branching) with rule-based transitions, built with a no-code visual editor; single-prompt agents are also supported.
systems.observability: Real-time call monitoring for QA, searchable and scored call transcription, unified logging across voice/SMS/chat channels, and a large prebuilt test-scenario suite for pathway regression testing.
systems.sdk_languages: Official Python SDK, a Node/TypeScript SDK (Admin server-side SDK plus a client-side Webchat SDK), and a full REST API.
systems.runs_on: Fully managed cloud; dedicated/on-prem/VPC infrastructure available for Enterprise.
systems.integration: Ships a bundled LLM/STT/TTS stack rather than a bring-your-own-provider model; pathway nodes call out to arbitrary external APIs and knowledge bases.

systems.name: Ultravox AI
systems.licence: Proprietary hosted service (built on the MIT-licensed, open-weight Ultravox speech-LLM, which is published separately on GitHub/Hugging Face and can be run independently of the hosted platform)
systems.price_note: Pay As You Go: first 30 min free, then $0.05/min for bundled voice (Ultravox's speech-native model plus hosted TTS, no separate STT step), up to 5 concurrent calls; SIP telephony is billed separately at $0.005/min. Pro plan ($100/mo): same $0.05/min voice rate, SIP drops to $0.0048/min, higher concurrency. Text-only "Realtime" API usage (Threads) is billed separately at $2/1M input tokens ($0 for cached input) and $15/1M output tokens. Enterprise is custom-priced.
systems.transport: WebRTC for browser/mobile clients, plus built-in integrations with major telephony providers and a documented SIP variant; no self-hosted transport layer of its own.
systems.tool_calling: Native "Tools" (function-calling) let the agent reach external systems mid-call, plus a separate Knowledge/RAG feature for grounding responses in custom content; both are dashboard- and API-configurable.
systems.self_host: This is Ultravox's managed hosted platform (telephony, SIP, dashboard, webhooks) — cloud-only, no self-host option for the platform itself; the vendor states it runs its own full inference stack. The underlying Ultravox speech-LLM (MIT-licensed) is published separately on GitHub/Hugging Face and can be run independently of this hosted product.
systems.best_for: Teams that want a speech-native agent (audio fed directly to the model, no separate ASR hop) for latency-sensitive phone/voice deployments, and are comfortable with a fully managed, telephony-integrated platform rather than self-hosting.
systems.watch: Fixie.ai rebranded to Ultravox AI on June 25, 2025 alongside the Ultravox v0.6 launch — older material and some SDK package names (ultravox-client, the ai.fixie Maven group) still carry the Fixie name, so don't assume a "Fixie.ai" reference is a different, older product. Also note the Pay-As-You-Go tier caps at 5 concurrent calls; real production volume needs the $100/mo Pro plan or an Enterprise quote.
systems.standout: Speech-native, audio-to-LLM architecture (built on the open-weight Ultravox model family, most recently v0.6/v0.7) skips the separate ASR step that cascaded platforms like Deepgram Voice Agent or Vapi/Retell run, which the vendor credits for ~150ms time-to-first-token and for preserving paralinguistic signal (tone, cadence) a text-transcription step would discard.
systems.architecture: Speech-native multimodal LLM (a pretrained text LLM backbone — Llama, Gemma, or Qwen variants — fused with a Whisper-large-v3-turbo speech encoder) that converts audio directly into the model's token space rather than transcribing to text first, wrapped in Ultravox's own hosted realtime/telephony infrastructure.
systems.observability: Conversation history with full audio recordings and transcripts, plus webhooks for realtime call events; no separately-named analytics/QA dashboard product (comparable to Vapi's Boards or Retell's post-call scoring) was found on the public site reviewed.
systems.sdk_languages: Official client SDKs for JavaScript/TypeScript (npm ultravox-client), Python (pip ultravox-client), Flutter, React Native, and Kotlin; a documented WebSocket protocol underlies all of them.
systems.runs_on: Ultravox's own managed cloud inference stack; no self-hosting option for the hosted platform itself.
systems.integration: Runs Ultravox's own speech-native model end-to-end rather than orchestrating third-party STT/LLM/TTS providers — the same vertically-integrated model as ElevenLabs Conversational AI or PolyAI, not the bring-your-own-provider pattern Vapi/Retell/Synthflow use.

systems.name: Synthflow
systems.price_note: Pricing has shifted to usage-based: as of current publication, synthflow.ai/pricing shows no flat legacy subscription tiers (the previously-marketed Starter/Pro/Growth/Agency plans, roughly $29-$1,250/mo, have been retired for new signups per multiple 2026 sources). New customers get Pay-As-You-Go component pricing: Voice Engine (TTS/STT) $0.09/min, LLM $0.00 (BYOK) to ~$0.05/min, telephony $0.00 (bring-your-own-carrier) to $0.02/min (Synthflow-managed Twilio) — roughly $0.13-0.24/min all-in. A separate Enterprise tier starts near $30,000/year (~$2,500/mo) for 10,000+ minutes/month, adding SIP trunking, unlimited concurrency, and forward-deployed-engineer onboarding. Some existing customers may remain grandfathered on legacy tiered plans.
systems.transport: Own carrier-grade telephony network plus bring-your-own SIP trunks; integrations with Cisco, Avaya, Genesys, and RingCentral contact-center systems.
systems.tool_calling: 200+ prebuilt integrations (CRMs, CCaaS platforms, calendars) plus custom API connections triggered from the flow builder, for real-time record updates and call routing.
systems.self_host: Managed cloud only; no self-hosting option. Forward-deployed engineers are offered for enterprise onboarding.
systems.best_for: Agencies and SMB teams that want a no-code visual flow builder with native white-label/reseller features (custom branding, sub-accounts, Stripe rebilling) to resell voice agents under their own brand.
systems.watch: Synthflow is BYOK for the underlying TTS/LLM/STT providers, so the subscription price does not cover those costs — real per-minute spend adds ElevenLabs (~$0.04-0.10/min), an LLM (~$0.01-0.03/min), and a transcriber (~$0.01/min) on top of the platform fee.
systems.standout: One of the most complete native agency/white-label toolsets in the category — custom domains, sub-accounts, feature visibility controls, and Stripe rebilling are all built in, not bolted on.
systems.architecture: Visual Flow Designer with modular subflows acting as specialized agents inside one logic tree; no-code by default, with an API available for custom automation.
systems.observability: Real-time visibility into calls/webhooks/APIs, automated QA scoring of conversations, KPI performance tracking, and call recording/analysis.
systems.sdk_languages: REST API and developer documentation for custom integrations; no dedicated client-side voice SDK is documented.
systems.runs_on: Fully managed, multi-region cloud infrastructure.
systems.integration: BYOK: brings your own ElevenLabs/TTS, LLM, and transcription provider rather than bundling one fixed stack.

systems.name: ElevenLabs Conversational AI
systems.price_note: Per-minute call billing on top of ElevenLabs' subscription tiers. As of the live pricing page (mid-2026), the published rate is a flat $0.08/min standard for calls across Free through Business tiers, with a $0.16/min burst rate above the plan's concurrency limit. (An earlier Feb-2025 promotional price of ~$0.10/min for Creator/Pro vs ~$0.08/min for annual Business no longer appears on the live pricing page — the tiers have since been unified to the flat $0.08/min rate.) LLM cost is billed separately.
systems.transport: Phone calls via third-party carrier integration (Twilio, Genesys, Vonage, Telnyx, Plivo) or any SIP-compatible PBX; a native WebSocket API; voice plus chat/SMS/WhatsApp channels.
systems.tool_calling: Workflow automation with prebuilt tool integrations (Zapier, Stripe, Cal.com, Zendesk, HubSpot, and 10+ others) for actions like payment processing, calendar management, and CRM updates inside a conversation.
systems.self_host: Fully managed cloud; APIs available for custom deployments, with elevated support and custom deployment options for enterprise.
systems.best_for: Teams already using ElevenLabs' TTS/voice-cloning stack who want to add a conversational agent layer without switching voice vendors, especially for multilingual (70+ language) deployments.
systems.watch: Published per-minute rates cover ElevenLabs' own voice/orchestration layer only — the LLM cost is billed separately on top, so total per-minute spend depends heavily on which model backs the agent.
systems.standout: Direct access to ElevenLabs' own TTS/voice-cloning models inside the agent, rather than a third-party voice bolted onto a generic orchestration layer.
systems.architecture: Agent + workflow model configured through a web dashboard or the WebSocket/REST API, with knowledge-base grounding and workflow automation built in.
systems.observability: Dashboard for tracking conversations, identifying gaps, and refining performance over time, with support for A/B testing and behavior correction.
systems.sdk_languages: JavaScript, React, Python, and iOS SDKs, plus a WebSocket API for custom integrations.
systems.runs_on: Fully managed cloud.
systems.integration: Requires a third-party telephony carrier (Twilio, Genesys, Vonage, Telnyx, Plivo) for phone connectivity — telephony is not native, unlike Retell/Vapi/Bland, which issue phone numbers directly.

systems.name: Deepgram Voice Agent API
systems.price_note: Bundled full stack (Deepgram's own STT + a pluggable LLM + Deepgram's own Aura TTS): $4.50/hr flat, i.e. the same $0.075/min as the Standard pay-as-you-go tier, billed on websocket connection time. Swapping in your own components discounts it further: Standard BYO TTS $0.065/min, Custom BYO LLM $0.059/min, Custom BYO LLM + TTS $0.050/min; a higher-accuracy Advanced STT tier runs $0.163/min standard or $0.122/min BYO TTS. A Growth plan cuts each of those up to ~20% (e.g. Standard to $0.068/min, Advanced to $0.146/min).
systems.transport: Native WebSocket API for real-time bidirectional audio streaming; telephony reach comes through documented carrier integrations (Twilio Media Streams for PSTN/SIP/WhatsApp, among others) rather than a SIP endpoint Deepgram operates itself.
systems.tool_calling: Native function-calling — the LLM layer can invoke developer-defined functions mid-conversation; Deepgram emits a function-call event, the developer's server executes it and returns the result over the same socket, and the agent incorporates it into its next turn.
systems.self_host: Managed cloud by default; also sold as dedicated single-tenant, in-VPC, or fully self-hosted (Docker/Kubernetes) deployments for enterprises with HIPAA/GDPR/data-residency requirements — broader deployment flexibility than the managed-cloud-only Retell/Bland/Synthflow, though the per-minute pricing above applies to the managed-cloud tier specifically.
systems.best_for: Teams that want Deepgram's own STT (Nova-3/Flux) and Aura TTS pre-wired together with a pluggable LLM in one billed-per-minute pipeline, without assembling separate STT/LLM/TTS vendors by hand.
systems.watch: The advertised $4.50/hr is exactly the Standard pay-as-you-go rate restated per hour ($0.075/min x 60), not a separate discount tier — the higher-accuracy Advanced STT tier more than doubles that to $0.163/min, and the cheapest combination (bring your own LLM AND your own TTS) floors out at $0.050/min, before any Growth-plan volume discount is applied on top.
systems.standout: Deepgram owns and runs every layer itself (Nova/Flux STT, Aura TTS) rather than repackaging third-party models, which is the pitch it markets directly against ElevenLabs Conversational AI (owns TTS but not STT) and OpenAI Realtime (bundled speech-to-speech with no per-layer swap) — a single-vendor stack with per-component BYO opt-outs instead of an all-or-nothing bundle.
systems.architecture: Cascaded pipeline exposed as a single voice-to-voice WebSocket connection: Deepgram's own Nova-3/Flux STT feeds a configurable LLM (Deepgram-hosted or bring-your-own), whose output is spoken by Deepgram's own Aura TTS, with built-in barge-in detection and turn-taking handled inside the same socket rather than as three separately-integrated services.
systems.observability: Not published as a dedicated dashboard product on the marketing site reviewed; conversation-level logs and function-call events are available over the same WebSocket session, but no standalone analytics/QA product comparable to Vapi's Boards or Retell's post-call scoring was found.
systems.sdk_languages: Server-side quickstarts and reference implementations in Python, JavaScript/Node.js, C#, and Go; the API itself is a documented WebSocket protocol, so any language with websocket support can integrate directly.
systems.runs_on: Deepgram's managed multi-region cloud by default; dedicated single-tenant, customer VPC, or self-hosted Docker/Kubernetes for enterprise compliance needs.
systems.integration: Deepgram's own Nova-3/Flux STT and Aura TTS wired in by default; supports bring-your-own LLM and/or bring-your-own TTS, each unlocking a lower per-minute rate than the fully-bundled tier.

systems.name: Pipecat Cloud
systems.licence: Proprietary hosted service (built on the BSD-2-Clause-licensed open-source Pipecat framework, which is separately self-hostable)
systems.price_note: Usage-metered: agent compute from $0.01/min active ($0.0005/min reserved) for agent-1x (higher tiers agent-2x $0.02/min active, agent-3x $0.03/min active); built-in SIP $0.003-$0.02/min, PSTN $0.018/min, $0.20/transfer event. Daily's pricing page discloses no public volume-discount schedule for agent-compute minutes; custom/enterprise pricing is available on request. One human + one agent minute is free when using a Pipecat Cloud-provisioned Daily key (free for 1:1 WebRTC voice sessions).
systems.transport: WebRTC (via Daily) and SmallWebRTC, plus built-in SIP and PSTN telephony, using the open-source Pipecat pipeline's transport layer.
systems.tool_calling: Inherits Pipecat's function-calling/context-aggregator components; connects to 80+ LLM/STT/TTS providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Deepgram, Cartesia, ElevenLabs, and others) for tool-augmented pipelines.
systems.self_host: This is the managed cloud deployment layer for the open-source, self-hostable Pipecat framework — the framework itself can run entirely on a customer's own infrastructure instead.
systems.best_for: Developer teams already building on the open-source Pipecat framework who want managed, auto-scaling, containerized production deployment (SIP/PSTN, monitoring, recording) without operating that infrastructure themselves.
systems.watch: This is a deployment layer for code you still write against the open-source Pipecat framework, not a no-code agent builder — the pipeline logic remains Python you author yourself, unlike Vapi/Retell/Bland/Synthflow's dashboard-first model. The BSD-2-Clause-licensed framework can also be self-hosted for free instead.
systems.standout: The lowest published per-minute agent-compute rate in this category, as a thin managed layer over a separately self-hostable open-source framework rather than a closed black box.
systems.architecture: Containerized deployment of open-source Pipecat pipelines (a frame-based ASR-to-LLM-to-TTS processing graph) onto managed, auto-scaling infrastructure with unlimited concurrency.
systems.observability: Built-in monitoring and telemetry, session recording, and persistent storage for session transcriptions.
systems.sdk_languages: Python (the underlying Pipecat framework's primary language); deployment tooling is documented around Python pipelines.
systems.runs_on: Daily's managed, multi-region cloud infrastructure.
systems.integration: Connects to 80+ third-party LLM/STT/TTS providers rather than bundling a fixed stack, with first-class integration into Daily's own WebRTC transport.

systems.name: LiveKit Cloud (Agents)
systems.licence: Proprietary hosted service (built on the Apache-2.0-licensed open-source LiveKit Agents framework, which is separately self-hostable)
systems.price_note: Metered: agent-session minutes at $0.01/min, WebRTC media minutes at $0.0004-0.0005/min, data transfer $0.10-0.12/GB above plan allotments. Four tiers: Build (free, 1,000 agent-session min/mo), Ship ($50/mo), Scale ($500/mo), Enterprise (custom).
systems.transport: WebRTC-based global media transport (LiveKit's core protocol), with SIP/PSTN telephony support for phone-based agents.
systems.tool_calling: Inherits the open-source LiveKit Agents framework's function-calling support; an Agent Builder is referenced for configuring agent behavior.
systems.self_host: This is the managed cloud deployment layer for the open-source, self-hostable LiveKit Agents framework — the framework can run entirely on a customer's own infrastructure instead.
systems.best_for: Developer teams already building on the open-source LiveKit Agents framework who want production-grade autoscaling, global edge placement, and built-in observability without running LiveKit's media servers themselves.
systems.watch: Like Pipecat Cloud, this is a deployment/infrastructure layer for the LiveKit Agents framework, not a no-code builder — you still write and version the agent code yourself, and the $0.01/min figure is session time only, before any LLM/STT/TTS provider costs.
systems.standout: Zero-downtime versioned deployments with single-click rollback, plus turn-by-turn conversation playback (synchronized transcripts and trace spans) for debugging production agents.
systems.architecture: Managed hosting for the open-source LiveKit Agents framework's Python/Node agent code, with load-balanced auto-scaling session placement across a global multi-region network (us-east, eu-central, ap-south).
systems.observability: Realtime dashboards with recordings, transcripts, traces, and full-stack logs per agent conversation, plus turn-by-turn conversation playback for debugging.
systems.sdk_languages: The same SDKs as the open-source LiveKit Agents framework: Python and Node.js/TypeScript agent SDKs, plus client SDKs for Web, iOS, Android, Flutter, React Native, and Unity.
systems.runs_on: LiveKit's managed, multi-region cloud infrastructure.
systems.integration: Deploys agents built against the open-source LiveKit Agents framework, which itself plugs into a wide range of third-party LLM/STT/TTS providers and turn-detection models.

systems.name: Cognigy.AI
systems.price_note: Enterprise sales only — no self-serve pricing published; quote-based.
systems.transport: Cognigy Voice Gateway for phone-based voice agents, plus chat/messaging channels; integrates with major contact-center platforms (Avaya, Genesys, NICE CXone, AWS, Microsoft, 8x8).
systems.tool_calling: An "Agentic AI" capability pillar covering tool/action execution; marketed toward orchestrating many agents per deployment (customer case studies cite double-digit counts of live agents per enterprise).
systems.self_host: Managed SaaS is the primary/recommended path, but on-premises and private-cloud self-hosted deployment via Kubernetes is publicly documented (docs.cognigy.com installation prerequisites) and shipped as a maintained public Helm chart (github.com/Cognigy/cognigy-ai-helm-chart) — Cognigy discourages it and won't support provisioning the cluster, but it is a real, publicly-surfaced option, not absent from the public site.
systems.best_for: Large enterprise contact centers that want conversational AI spanning voice AND chat/messaging under one platform, typically deployed through systems integrators rather than self-serve signup.
systems.watch: Cognigy was acquired by NICE (NASDAQ: NICE) in a deal that closed September 8, 2025; the product now operates as "NiCE Cognigy," offered both standalone and folded into NICE's CXone Mpower platform — evaluate roadmap, pricing, and support continuity in light of the acquisition. Pricing, SLAs, and most technical specifics (transport protocols, tool-calling API shape, SDK languages) remain gated behind a sales conversation — almost nothing beyond marketing-page claims is independently verifiable from the public site.
systems.standout: Positions itself as one platform for voice AND chat/messaging conversational AI (not voice-only), aimed at contact centers already running Avaya/Genesys/NICE infrastructure.
systems.architecture: Not disclosed in technical detail on the public site — described only at the marketing level as "AI Ops & Orchestration."
systems.observability: "Insights & Analytics" and "AI Ops & Orchestration" are referenced as built-in monitoring/analytics; implementation details are not public.
systems.sdk_languages: Not published on the public site.
systems.runs_on: Managed cloud (AWS EKS / Azure AKS recommended); on-premises or private-cloud Kubernetes self-hosting is also documented and technically supported, though Cognigy actively discourages it and provides no provisioning support for it.
systems.integration: Built for integration with existing enterprise contact-center stacks (Avaya, Genesys, NICE CXone, AWS, Microsoft, 8x8) rather than sold as a standalone telephony product.

systems.name: PolyAI
systems.price_note: Enterprise sales only — no self-serve pricing published; demo/consultation required.
systems.transport: Voice-native dialog agents for phone-based customer engagement, with multi-channel support; specific telephony protocols are not published.
systems.tool_calling: Documented in the Agent Development Kit (ADK) reference: "Functions" are Python building blocks that call external/backend APIs (a published example calls `external_api.get_booking(booking_ref, include_history)`), route on conversation state, and transfer calls; multi-agent hand-offs are documented separately as "Handoffs." The integrations catalog also lists custom and MCP connectors. ("Analyst Agents" — natural-language querying of interaction data — is an observability feature, not evidence of tool-calling.)
systems.self_host: Managed/hosted platform; no self-hosting option.
systems.best_for: Large multilingual enterprise contact centers that want a vertically-integrated voice stack tuned for accents, background noise, and interruptions in high-volume phone support.
systems.watch: PolyAI builds its own ASR and LLM rather than plugging into third-party providers — the vertical integration is the pitch, but it also means a buyer cannot swap in a different model or voice provider the way they can on Vapi/Retell/Synthflow.
systems.standout: A fully proprietary, vertically-integrated voice stack (own ASR, LLM, and neural TTS) trained specifically on enterprise call-center conversation data, rather than orchestrating third-party providers.
systems.architecture: Agent Studio (a web-based, business-user-facing builder) plus an Agent Development Kit (ADK) for developer-authored agents, on top of a proprietary end-to-end voice stack rather than a pluggable-provider orchestration layer.
systems.observability: "Analytics & Insights" with visibility into agent decisions, plus "Analyst Agents" for natural-language querying of interaction data.
systems.sdk_languages: Agent Development Kit (ADK), documented at polyai.github.io/adk.
systems.runs_on: Managed cloud.
systems.integration: Runs a proprietary ASR ("Owl")/LLM ("Raven")/neural-TTS stack built in-house rather than orchestrating third-party STT/LLM/TTS providers — the opposite integration model from Vapi/Retell/Synthflow.

systems.name: jambonz
systems.licence: MIT (source, and the v0.9.x branch is fully free); v10+ requires a paid Standard/OEM licence key for production use
systems.price_note: Self-hosted: per-concurrent-session or flat-fee licence for v10+ (free trial and extended free tier for students/hobbyists/pre-revenue startups); v0.9.x remains free (security/bug fixes only). Hosted jambonz cloud priced per concurrent session.
systems.transport: Native SIP trunking; PSTN via your own carrier SIP trunk; WebRTC via the jambonz client SDK. RTP media handled internally by the platform.
systems.tool_calling: Native `llm` verb manages realtime voice-AI sessions for 8 vendors (OpenAI Realtime/GPT Live, Gemini Live, Deepgram Voice Agent, ElevenLabs, Ultravox, AssemblyAI Voice Agent, xAI Voice Agent) with built-in tool-calling orchestration: jambonz emits an `llm:tool-call` message to your `toolHook` webhook and you return results via `session.sendToolOutput()`. You still implement each tool's actual logic — jambonz doesn't execute functions itself — but the call-routing/session plumbing is a native platform primitive, not something you build from scratch.
systems.self_host: Self-hosted (Docker, bare-metal, or air-gapped) or jambonz-hosted cloud
systems.best_for: Teams that need full SIP/PSTN call control (routing, transfer, recording) with swappable STT/TTS/LLM, self-hosted or in a private/regulated cloud, and are willing to pay for the current major version
systems.watch: v10 and later require a purchased licence key for production — only the older 0.9.x branch is unconditionally free/MIT (maintenance fixes only going forward). Read the licensing-change post before assuming free self-hosting: https://blog.jambonz.org/why-were-introducing-a-commercial-license
systems.architecture: SIP feature server (Node.js) fronted by drachtio's SIP stack; declarative, webhook-driven call-control 'verbs'; STT/TTS/LLM are swappable per call.
systems.observability: Built-in call logs, recordings, and a web portal for call tracing; no LLM/agent-conversation tracing beyond call-level logs.
systems.sdk_languages: Node.js primary SDK; call-control is webhook-based and language-agnostic
systems.runs_on: Self-hosted Linux/Docker, or jambonz's own cloud
systems.integration: For traditional (non-realtime) call flows, bring your own STT/TTS/LLM provider per call via webhook handlers. For realtime voice AI, the native `llm` verb bundles and manages the full session (audio streaming, turn-taking, tool-call routing) for 8 supported vendors — session orchestration is handled by the platform, not entirely left to your application as the row implies.
systems.adoption: Vendor states deployment at several Fortune 500 companies plus SMBs/startups; ~97 GitHub stars on the core jambonz-feature-server repo — a small, niche-telephony project by star count, not a mainstream-framework metric

systems.name: drachtio
systems.price_note: Free, open source; no hosted/managed offering — self-host only
systems.transport: Raw SIP (proxy, UAC/UAS, back-to-back user agent); no PSTN termination of its own — bring your own SIP trunk/carrier for PSTN reach
systems.tool_calling: None — drachtio is a low-level SIP signaling framework, not an AI/agent layer. LLM tool-calling is entirely your own application code.
systems.self_host: Self-hosted only
systems.best_for: Developers who need raw, low-level SIP control (proxies, B2BUAs, custom routing logic) as the signaling layer under a custom-built voice-AI stack, rather than an off-the-shelf agent framework
systems.watch: Pure SIP signaling only — no STT/TTS/LLM, no PSTN termination, and no agent primitives are included. Everything above the SIP layer, including how you get a phone number onto it, is your own build.
systems.standout: sofia-SIP-based like FreeSWITCH, but exposed as familiar Express-style Node.js middleware instead of a monolithic PBX config
systems.architecture: drachtio-server: a C++ SIP user agent built on the sofia-SIP stack (the same stack FreeSWITCH uses), controlled over a TCP connection by drachtio-srf, a Node.js library styled after Express/Connect middleware.
systems.observability: None built in beyond standard SIP-level logging; no conversation/LLM observability
systems.sdk_languages: Node.js (drachtio-srf); lower-level drachtio-client bindings
systems.runs_on: Self-hosted Linux (Docker images published); no GPU required
systems.integration: None built in — commonly paired with a custom Node.js app (or jambonz, which is built on top of it) for the AI/STT/TTS/LLM layer.
systems.adoption: 331 GitHub stars on drachtio-server, 220 on drachtio-srf (verified via GitHub API, last pushed July 2026); it is the SIP layer jambonz itself is built on

systems.name: OpenSIPS AI Voice Connector (Community Edition)
systems.price_note: Free, open source (Community Edition); OpenSIPS itself is a free open-source SIP server
systems.transport: SIP (OpenSIPS acting as a back-to-back user agent); captures and injects RTP media directly into and out of the AI engine
systems.tool_calling: Delegated entirely to whichever AI engine is plugged in (e.g., OpenAI Realtime's own function calling) — the connector itself has no tool-calling logic
systems.self_host: Self-hosted only
systems.best_for: Teams already running OpenSIPS who want the shortest path from a live SIP trunk to a realtime speech-to-speech AI engine (OpenAI Realtime, Deepgram Voice Agent) without hand-building the SIP/RTP bridge
systems.watch: Last GitHub push found was roughly 9 months before this review (pushed_at 2025-11-04) — verify current commit activity before relying on the Community Edition for production. The claim that OpenSIPS sells a separate paid/enterprise edition of this specific AI Voice Connector could not be independently verified — no such product is mentioned on opensips.org or in the connector's own docs, and no second public repo exists under the OpenSIPS org; OpenSIPS the company does sell general commercial SIP support/services, which may be the source of confusion.
systems.architecture: Modular Python application sitting behind an OpenSIPS instance: OpenSIPS handles SIP call signaling as a B2BUA, and the connector captures/relays RTP to the configured AI-engine 'flavor', injecting the response back into the live call.
systems.observability: None built in beyond standard OpenSIPS/SIP logging
systems.sdk_languages: Python
systems.runs_on: Self-hosted Linux; requires a running OpenSIPS instance alongside it
systems.integration: Ships 'flavors' for OpenAI (OpenAI Realtime API, speech-to-speech), Deepgram Native (Deepgram Voice Agent API, speech-to-speech), Deepgram (Deepgram STT + ChatGPT + Deepgram TTS), and Azure (Azure STT + ChatGPT + Azure TTS) — you pick the AI engine, the connector wires the SIP/RTP side. Note: there is no 'Deepgram STT + Azure TTS' flavor; the same-vendor Deepgram STT+TTS combo is a distinct flavor from Azure's.
systems.adoption: 83 GitHub stars, 105 commits (verified via GitHub API)

systems.name: Agent Voice Response (AVR)
systems.price_note: Free, open source; no paid tier for the core project
systems.transport: Asterisk AudioSocket/RTP — PSTN and SIP reach depend on how you've configured the Asterisk/FreePBX instance AVR sits behind
systems.tool_calling: Depends on the plugged-in LLM connector (e.g. avr-llm-openai, avr-llm-openai-assistant support OpenAI-style function calling); AVR itself adds no separate tool-calling layer
systems.self_host: Self-hosted only
systems.best_for: Teams standardized on Asterisk/FreePBX who want a ready-made, MIT-licensed microservices pipeline (ASR/LLM/TTS) instead of writing the AudioSocket bridge themselves
systems.watch: Scoped tightly to Asterisk via AudioSocket — not a general SIP framework. Individual provider-connector repos vary widely in how recently they've been touched (some from 2024, some from this year), so check the specific connector you need before committing.
systems.architecture: Composable microservices — Core, ASR, LLM, TTS, VAD each a separate Dockerized service — but only Core speaks Asterisk's AudioSocket protocol directly; Core then talks to the ASR/LLM/TTS services over HTTP APIs (WebSocket for speech-to-speech/STS integrations), with the provider used at each stage swappable via docker-compose configuration.
systems.observability: None built in beyond per-service logs; no dedicated tracing UI
systems.sdk_languages: Node.js/JavaScript microservices; deployed via Docker Compose
systems.runs_on: Self-hosted Linux + Asterisk/FreePBX, via Docker Compose
systems.integration: ~30 small provider-connector repos under the org: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, ElevenLabs, Deepgram, Kokoro, Vosk, Rime, Coqui TTS, n8n, plus OpenAI/Deepgram/Ultravox speech-to-speech
systems.adoption: 96 GitHub stars on avr-infra, 27 on avr-app, 21 on avr-vad (verified via GitHub API across the org's ~30 repos)

systems.name: SignalWire AI Agents SDK (SWAIG)
systems.price_note: SDK is free/MIT; placing calls requires a SignalWire account and its usage-based telephony pricing (numbers, PSTN minutes, SIP)
systems.transport: SIP, PSTN, and WebRTC, all via the SignalWire platform — phone numbers, SIP endpoints, and browser/app calls route through the same agent logic
systems.tool_calling: SWAIG (SignalWire AI Gateway) — native function-calling: the agent can call HTTP-POST-backed functions mid-call to send SMS, query a CRM, start a recording, join a conference, or transfer to a human
systems.self_host: Hybrid — the agent code/SDK is self-hosted (or served via SignalWire's Agent Builder), but SIP/PSTN termination runs on SignalWire's managed telephony platform
systems.best_for: Teams building multi-step or multi-agent phone workflows (qualify caller, transfer to a specialist agent, hand off to a human) who want native function-calling and state-tracked call flows on carrier-grade SIP/PSTN, without hand-rolling the call-state machine
systems.watch: The SDK's own canonical GitHub link (github.com/signalwire/signalwire-agents), cited by SignalWire's own docs and the PyPI page, returned 404 at time of research. The package itself is real and current (PyPI v1.1.0, March 2026) and SignalWire's docs site is live — but verify the repo link before republishing it further.
systems.architecture: Python SDK where agents are self-hosted microservices (SWML documents) that SignalWire's telephony platform invokes; a 'Contexts and Steps' system layers structured, state-tracked workflows on top of a base prompt so each step gets a fresh context instead of an ever-growing history.
systems.observability: SignalWire publishes an official self-hosted observability tool, post_prompt_viewer (github.com/signalwire/post_prompt_viewer): a searchable call index with per-turn transcript, latency/confidence, a SWAIG function-call inspector, a timeline event viewer, and cost/token telemetry (tokens, TTS chars, ASR minutes) -- run against your own post_prompt_url, not a hosted SaaS dashboard -- plus Contexts/Steps state transitions and standard call logs.
systems.sdk_languages: Python is the primary/most mature SDK; the same AI Agents framework (SWAIG, Contexts/Steps, AgentBase) is also published for Ruby, C++, Go, Java, TypeScript, PHP, Perl, C# (.NET), and Rust under the SignalWire org.
systems.runs_on: Self-hosted (any Python host) for the agent logic; SignalWire's cloud for telephony
systems.integration: Native multi-agent support via Contexts/Steps (in-agent workflow navigation, e.g. swml_change_context) plus explicit transfer primitives -- swml_transfer() to hand off to another AI agent, connect() to transfer to a human/phone number -- but SignalWire's own docs do not state that conversation state (global_data, transcript, etc.) is preserved across either kind of transfer; that part of the claim is unverified.
systems.adoption: PyPI package at v1.1.0 (March 2026); vendor markets it as production-ready voice AI

systems.name: Twilio ConversationRelay
systems.licence: Proprietary — hosted service under Twilio's Terms of Service/Acceptable Use Policy, no source available
systems.price_note: $0.07/min for ConversationRelay orchestration itself; voice/PSTN minutes are calculated and billed separately under your standard Twilio Voice plan, as are any STT/TTS/LLM costs you bring
systems.transport: PSTN and WebRTC (via the Twilio Voice JS SDK), confirmed in Twilio's ConversationRelay documentation via the <Connect><ConversationRelay> TwiML noun and a single WebSocket interface to your server. SIP is not documented as a supported transport for ConversationRelay in Twilio's TwiML reference, WebSocket message reference, onboarding guide, or Elastic SIP Trunking docs.
systems.tool_calling: No native tool/function-calling mechanism exists in the ConversationRelay protocol -- documented WebSocket message types are setup, prompt, dtmf, interrupt, error (incoming) and text, play, sendDigits, language, end (outgoing), with no tool-call type among them. Because the architecture is bring-your-own-LLM, any function/tool calling happens inside the developer's own WebSocket server via their chosen LLM's own tool-calling API (OpenAI's, Anthropic's, etc.) -- this is not a Twilio-native feature, and no official Twilio guide demonstrating one was found (only third-party community repos on GitHub).
systems.self_host: Fully managed/hosted only — not self-hostable
systems.best_for: Teams already on Twilio Voice who want STT/TTS/media handling done for them and just want to plug in an LLM, targeting sub-second latency
systems.watch: No self-hosting option, and the $0.07/min orchestration fee stacks on top of standard Twilio Voice/PSTN charges plus whatever LLM (and any third-party STT/TTS) you still choose to bring.
systems.standout: Twilio reports <0.5s median / <0.725s p95 latency (Twilio's own benchmark; results may vary per their own disclaimer); one WebSocket interface spans PSTN and browser WebRTC. SIP support is not documented by Twilio for ConversationRelay.
systems.architecture: Managed relay: Twilio owns the media/STT/TTS pipeline and streams transcripts/events to your WebSocket server, which runs the LLM and returns text or actions back — bring-your-own-LLM, Twilio-managed everything else.
systems.observability: Integrates with Twilio Conversational Intelligence for post-call transcripts and insights
systems.sdk_languages: Language-agnostic WebSocket protocol; official quickstarts in Node.js and Python
systems.runs_on: Twilio's cloud; your LLM logic runs wherever your WebSocket server lives
systems.adoption: Twilio Voice is one of the largest CPaaS platforms; ConversationRelay is listed operational across multiple Twilio regions (US1, AU1, IE1) and appears on Twilio's public Voice pricing page, consistent with general availability. The claim of 'multiple published Twilio reference architectures (AWS/Bedrock, Mistral, Claude)' could not be verified -- no official Twilio blog posts or docs matching that description were found; only third-party/community GitHub demos combine ConversationRelay with Bedrock or Claude.

systems.name: Telnyx AI Voice Agents (SIP Attach)
systems.licence: Proprietary — hosted service under Telnyx's Terms of Service, no source available
systems.price_note: $0.05/min covers orchestration, hosted STT, and hosted TTS; LLM tokens are billed separately (roughly $0.004/min typical on Telnyx-hosted open models, or pass-through rates for Anthropic/OpenAI), and telephony starts at $0.0032/min — a typical production agent runs about $0.056/min all-in
systems.transport: Native SIP endpoint registration via 'SIP Attach' (the agent can join an existing PBX/UC dial plan directly), plus PSTN and standard SIP trunking
systems.tool_calling: Python (telnyx-agent-toolkit) and TypeScript (@telnyx/agent-toolkit) expose Telnyx APIs as tool-calling functions for OpenAI's Agents SDK, LangChain, CrewAI, and Vercel's AI SDK; Telnyx also runs a hosted MCP server at api.telnyx.com/v2/mcp
systems.self_host: Fully managed/hosted only — not self-hostable
systems.best_for: Teams that want the SIP trunk, PSTN termination, and AI orchestration from a single carrier-owned vendor, or that need an AI agent to register as a SIP endpoint inside an existing PBX dial plan rather than answering a newly issued number
systems.watch: Fully proprietary and hosted — same single-vendor lock-in tradeoff as any carrier-bundled AI layer, with no self-host path.
systems.standout: SIP Attach lets the agent register as a SIP endpoint on an existing PBX/softswitch dial plan instead of only fronting a new Telnyx phone number
systems.architecture: Carrier-hosted voice AI orchestration layer (STT + LLM routing + TTS) running directly on Telnyx's own SIP/PSTN network; 'SIP Attach' lets the agent register as a SIP endpoint inside an existing PBX/softswitch dial plan rather than only fronting a Telnyx-issued number.
systems.observability: Telnyx documents a Langfuse-based observability integration (developers.telnyx.com/docs/inference/ai-assistants/agent-observability): connecting an assistant to Langfuse traces every LLM call (input, output, model, token usage), every tool execution (name, args, result), and groups conversation turns via deterministic trace IDs, all viewable in the Langfuse dashboard alongside latency and cost. This is a real, separately-documented tracing/observability capability, not merely standard call logs.
systems.sdk_languages: Python and TypeScript agent toolkits; REST API
systems.runs_on: Telnyx's own Tier-1 carrier network
systems.integration: Multi-participant/multi-agent calls via an Invite tool, plus an Agent Handoff tool with unified or per-agent voice modes for transferring between agents mid-call
systems.adoption: Telnyx markets itself on carrier-grade infrastructure across 40+ countries; figures are vendor-published, not independently audited

systems.name: Voximplant Voice AI
systems.licence: Proprietary — hosted service under Voximplant's Terms of Service, no source available
systems.price_note: $0.004/min for Voice AI connectivity to a WebSocket-based engine (Deepgram, OpenAI, Gemini, ElevenLabs Agents, Ultravox, etc.), billed in 15-second increments; telephony billed separately, from $0.005/min inbound and $0.014/min outbound
systems.transport: PSTN (100+ countries per vendor's own phone-number coverage claim; company-wide the vendor separately claims to operate in 190+ countries), SIP trunking and registration (interop with carriers, PBXs, SBCs), WebRTC, mobile, and WhatsApp Business Calling
systems.tool_calling: Code-driven agent orchestration (JavaScript scenario logic via VoxEngine). Vendor docs list Deepgram, OpenAI, Gemini, ElevenLabs, Ultravox, Cartesia, Grok, and Azure as an undifferentiated set of built-in 'Voice AI connectors' — function-calling/tool-calling for any of them is not documented in the vendor materials reviewed.
systems.self_host: Fully managed/hosted only — not self-hostable
systems.best_for: High call-volume teams for whom per-minute orchestration cost is the deciding factor, and who are comfortable with a fully hosted, code-scripted (not visual) CPaaS
systems.watch: No self-hosting option. The 'Voice AI Orchestration Platform' branding (voximplant.ai) is a newer product layer on top of the older Voximplant CPaaS/SIP-trunking business (voximplant.com) — check which product page and pricing table you're actually reading.
systems.architecture: Serverless, code-driven CPaaS scenario engine (VoxEngine JavaScript) that wires phone/SIP/WebRTC media to a pluggable STT/LLM/TTS pipeline or a speech-to-speech engine.
systems.observability: Not documented in the vendor materials reviewed
systems.sdk_languages: JavaScript (VoxEngine scenario scripting); REST APIs for platform management
systems.runs_on: Voximplant's cloud (15 globally-distributed data centers per vendor)
systems.integration: Built-in connectors (vendor's own term, applied uniformly) to Deepgram, OpenAI, Gemini, ElevenLabs Agents, Ultravox, Cartesia, Grok, and Microsoft Azure, supporting speech-to-speech, half-cascade, or full-cascade STT/LLM/TTS pipelines — the vendor's docs do not single out Deepgram or OpenAI as more 'native' than the other listed providers.
systems.adoption: Marketed for call centers and automation providers; no independent usage figures found beyond vendor materials

gaps: Cognigy.AI and PolyAI publish almost nothing beyond marketing-page claims — both carry verification: vendor-claim and several fields marked "not disclosed" or "not published on the public site" rather than a guessed number.

Two rows (Telnyx AI Voice Agents, Voximplant Voice AI) rely primarily on vendor documentation with no independent adoption or usage figures found — flagged in their own watch/adoption fields rather than silently presented as neutral facts.
This catalog does not attempt to be exhaustive — it covers 27 systems found through a structured research pass across three categories, not every voice-agent orchestration tool that exists.
